speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment for the Implementation of the Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS), how will NEA ensure that (i) the locations of all BCRS vending machines are known to consumers and (ii) retailers and shops do not sell beverages in non-returnable containers at the same price as returnable containers to consumers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in respect of the Beverage Container Return Scheme (a) what measures will be put in place to mitigate the impact of potential price increases on consumers, particularly for products from smaller producers; and (b) what assistance will be provided to vulnerable residents not living near return points to claim their container deposits.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether NEA took reference from other countries in designing the Beverage Container Return Scheme; (b) whether NEA has considered alternatives which could have a lower cost impact on producers and consumers; and (c) how will NEA ensure that producers and consumers are not adversely and severely impacted.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This scheme was debated three years ago during the Second Reading of the Resource Sustainability (Amendment) Bill and Members had expressed support for the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Engagements and discussions with industry and the public had started even earlier.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The scheme was first proposed by a Recycle Right Citizens’ Workgroup in 2019 to increase household recycling rates and reduce contamination in the recycling bins.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The amount of packaging waste generated in Singapore forms one third of our domestic waste generated and our overall recycling rate remains low.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The BCRS aims to increase the recycling of beverage containers using an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) concept.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And this is the second such scheme to be introduced in Singapore, building on our experience with the e-waste recycling programme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The scheme features a deposit paid at the point of purchase to incentivise consumers to return their containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: By nudging consumers to make a small change in their lifestyle, we hope to increase recycling of beverage containers and spark a change in our recycling habits.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In designing the scheme, we studied the experiences of other jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Schemes in Norway, Denmark and Lithuania have achieved high collection rates, and one common factor was having an industry-led, not-for-profit entity run the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have adopted a similar approach in Singapore, because the industry stakeholders are best placed to determine the most effective way to recover used beverage containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are also incentivised to operate the scheme efficiently and effectively to ensure that the cost impact on producers is manageable.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The scheme operator, BCRS Ltd, was formed by the industry and is governed by a Board that has both large and small producer representatives, comprising Coca-Cola Singapore Beverages, F&N Foods, Pokka, Wanin Industries and Chia Khim Lee Food Industries.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Licensed by the National Environment Agency (NEA), they are required to report the amount of 10-cent deposits collected from the producers and refunded to the consumers in their annual report for public accountability.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Several Members asked questions about the cost of the scheme and the effect on beverage prices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Such containers will bear a deposit mark for easy identification.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Consumers will pay this 10 cents at the point of purchase and obtain their refund when they return the containers for recycling.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This fee covers the logistics to collect and recycle the containers and is comparable to fees in other jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: From our engagements with stakeholders, producers of about 80% of beverage containers can incorporate the deposit mark and barcode requirements directly on their containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Beyond the once-off implementation cost, these producers should see costs per container close to the producer fee of three to four cents, which should keep compliance costs low for most drinks sold.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some producers may need to, or may choose to, place a sticker on their containers, instead of changing the design of the container, in order to comply with the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The cost of stickering will vary, depending on the quantity of containers put to market and how their supply chains are organised.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some can do so for about three cents per container, if done at source overseas and at scale.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For small quantities done locally, the cost to the producer would be higher.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We appreciate that some producers may find the transition more challenging.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: NEA and the scheme operator BCRS Ltd have been engaging both large and small producers regularly and providing practical support to help them come on board.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to be flexible and supportive to producers who reach out to BCRS Ltd to help address their concerns.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Over time, we expect producers to work with BCRS Ltd to optimise their processes and find cost effective ways to meet their responsibility to the environment.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The consumer pricing of beverages is a complex and commercial decision.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Consumer demand patterns and marketing strategies will also affect the price.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have designed the scheme to be run as efficiently as possible, with a low cost to producers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Any cost pass-through to consumers will likely be further moderated by price competition among industry players, as consumers have a wide variety of choices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This has been the experience in some jurisdictions that have implemented this, where studies found that the introduction of deposit return schemes did not have a significant direct impact on beverage prices or beverage sales.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Members have also asked about the accessibility of our return point network.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At launch in April, the public can return their empty plastic and metal beverage containers bearing the deposit mark at over 1,000 Reverse Vending Machines (RVMs) located across Singapore to obtain a 10-cent refund.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These RVMs will be located at larger supermarkets and other publicly accessible locations with high footfall, such as void decks of HDB blocks and some hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: BCRS Ltd will provide more details on the RVM locations in the coming weeks.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We aim to double the number of return points to 2,000 RVMs within the first year of implementation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to create a scheme that works for all of us.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We recognise that some seniors and vulnerable members of the community may require additional assistance to adapt to the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A key focus for us in the coming weeks is to work closely with all stakeholders to build understanding and support for the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will be reaching out to grassroots organisations, schools, youth groups, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and corporate partners to share how the scheme works and why it matters.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Many are already champions of our sustainability initiatives and I hope will continue to advocate for how BCRS is a very important step in our journey to look after our land, our resources and our environment.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are also in discussions with other key stakeholders, including coffeeshops and smaller retailers, to help them understand the scheme and explain it to consumers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This includes posters and collaterals to assist in distinguishing new beverage containers bearing the deposit mark, from older or non-regulated beverages that are not subject to the deposit.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The beverage container return scheme is a significant step forward in Singapore’s recycling journey.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It will take time for all of us to adjust.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will not get everything right from the start.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We ask for feedback, suggestions and understanding as we transit to this new way of recycling.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As we gather more data, we will refine and improve the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need everyone’s support to make this scheme a success.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to thank the producers who have helped to bring the scheme to where it is today and call upon those who have yet to register for the scheme to come forward and do their part for the environment.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The scheme cannot succeed without the support of our residents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I encourage Members of the House to rally their communities to participate actively, and extend a helping hand to those who may need assistance in returning their containers, as we all do our part for Singapore’s sustainability journey.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: First, we expect this collection of return containers, with over 1,000, to even in future, 2,000 return points to be quite a substantial operational and logistical effort.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: What is the estimated additional manpower that is needed for collection and transportation of all these collected containers?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: And related to this, my second supplementary question: how would consumers be protected?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Should the cost of drinks go beyond the three to four cents of operational costs, as imputed in these logistical operations, will that lead to much more expensive drinks in future for consumers?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They also maintain the cleanliness and operations of the machines.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The reverse logistics operators are companies and entities that are already well known to us.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are actually part of our public waste collection and Town Council operations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are they are not new companies being set up just for this purpose.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not have a specific answer in terms of the number of man hours.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is something that will be adjusted over time, depending on which RVMs require frequent clearance and which ones only require clearance once per day.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we will be watching this closely and we are working with the companies to make sure that their operations can be done smoothly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have to make sure that the machines maintain their up-time as a service to the residents, so that the ability to return these beverage containers is always there.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To her second question about protection for consumers, there are several reasons to have some degree of confidence in what is going to happen moving forward.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The first is the experience in other jurisdictions where the introduction of such schemes has not led to an increase in price of beverage containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: More than 50 jurisdictions around the world have introduced similar schemes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, in designing our scheme, we took reference from those lessons around the world and started with our BCRS, which is industry-led.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They have been quite engaging and open about this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a long tail of smaller producers that will face some challenges, and as I have explained, we will be flexible and supportive to assist these businesses in dealing with the transition and will try to help them come on board.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The protection for the consumers is that our consumers are quite discriminatory and they will adjust purchasing behaviour if there is indeed some attempt to extract excessive profits through this process.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My clarification for the Senior Minister of State is this: I thank him for his response that there will be about 1,000 RVMs set up country-wide, with an aim to increase to about 2,000.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But in context, there are about 15,000 vending machines in Singapore and I believe a significant number of them are vending drinks.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, in comparison, the ratio is about 1,000:15,000.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The way in which we are doing it, this phased approach, is indeed to then learn about how best to deploy, where best to deploy and how best to then have ambassadors come and assist people.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we are deploying 1,000 machines together with operations to have people stand by the machines at certain times of the day to assist seniors particularly, but also anybody who is asking for help.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will learn from that experience to decide how we should deploy the next 1,000 machines and where we should deploy them.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Again, we are learning from the experience of jurisdictions overseas.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are also learning from the experience here in Singapore, where we had about 50 RVMs operate through a pilot programme over four years.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We collected about 16 million containers through that process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The operators of that pilot are also one of our return point network operators and on the board of BCRS Ltd.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Nevertheless, we are going to look at the data very closely and make sure that we make the RVMs accessible to Singaporeans so that they can return their beverage containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In other words, you only have 10% of your time for cleaning, clearing the beverage containers and doing repairs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For the rest of the time, it needs to be available.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is a metric that we will be watching very closely, and BCRS Ltd will be watching in terms of their contractual arrangements with the return point network operators.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have two clarifications for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, could the Ministry provide additional grants and support, including on a longer-term basis, for smaller drinks producers to help defray the costs of complying with the scheme?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, would the Ministry consider waiving the requirement to have the deposit mark after the transition period, given that there should be sufficient public awareness by then and retailers no longer need to distinguish products with and without the 10-cent deposit?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are currently providing a grant of $2,500.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That grant is given to all registered producers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But it is sized to especially address the needs of the smaller producers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, that is how we have sized the grant.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are prepared to exercise flexibility and look at further support, but we also have to recognise that the purpose of this scheme is to shift some of the responsibility to the producer.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Today, if we purchase a beverage container, the entire responsibility for recycling that beverage container rests with the consumer.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What we want is to shift some of that responsibility to the producer, so that they think about their supply chains, about the materials that are used and about how they commissioned their product and put it to market.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we will consider these factors, but in general, we are prepared to be flexible and supportive in order to make sure that this scheme includes as much material as possible that we can successfully recycle.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Valerie Lim — Yes, Senior Minister of State?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think Ms Pereira had a second question that I have not yet answered, about waiving the deposit mark after the transition.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, not all beverage containers will be covered by the scheme and a consumer will need to know that the beverage container that they have in their hand is ineligible for the deposit.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the deposit mark will be necessary for some time as the scheme does not cover 100% of beverage containers, and we want to make sure that consumers know which ones will attract the deposit and hence, be eligible for use at the RVMs for refunds.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The first is whether the deposit value will be revealed over time and what criteria will trigger such a review?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And for the second supplementary question, what is the increase in the national recycling rate that we expect to see as a result of this scheme?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, whether the 10-cent deposit amount may be subsequently reviewed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we will review the scheme as we go along.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The quantum of the deposit in the 50 jurisdictions that we have studied does vary and some are significantly more than what we have here in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is something we will review as we go along, to ensure that the scheme is effective.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As for the recycling rate, we are hoping that we can get a good recycling rate of beverage containers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of the best schemes in the world have recycling rates of over 90%.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Most of them that we have studied, that we are trying to emulate, are closer to the 70% to 80% range.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is the sort of recycling rate that we would be hoping to achieve through this process.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The deposit rate is fully refundable at 10 cents, but I believe media reports have put the projected price increase at 25 to 60 cents.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, the difference is about 15 to 50 cents of permanent compliance costs, which the vending machine will not return.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, what assessment has been made of this non-refundable portion as a share of income for lower-income households?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question: the only current confirmed refund method is EZ-Link.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, can the Senior Minister of State confirm that the cash refund or cash voucher refund option will be available at all return points from Day 1.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The third supplementary question: a lot of parallel importers face $40,000 a month of fees under the scheme.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: With the transition grant at $2,500, that is quite disproportionate.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, these parallel importers are the companies that bring the cheapest drinks onto the market.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Has the Ministry assessed the risk that this scheme eliminates the discount beverage segment entirely?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: And final supplementary question: I note that the Senior Minister of State has said that they will monitor to see if the price increases will go beyond three to four cents.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But as we all know, price increases are sticky.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, what will the Government do if the price increases go beyond three to four cents?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On his first point, he quotes it as a projection.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The 25 to 60 cents was a media report from a handful of producers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, there will be smaller producers who, because of their supply chain or the size of their operations, will have higher challenges and we are prepared to be flexible and supportive, as explained.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The grant that we sized already covers about one-quarter of the producers and especially those that have put to market of less than 50,000 units.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are hoping to use digital means and BCRS Ltd will be announcing the other means for refund in the future.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have indeed engaged with a variety of importers, including some of the smallest importers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think the smallest producer that we have directly engaged has a put to market of 1,000 units.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are trying to understand their challenges, and we are trying to find ways to help them participate in this scheme while remaining viable as a business.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: What will the Government do if price increases —

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will look to see what are the factors that have led to that.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Since small beverage producers may likely pass the compliance cost to consumers, what percentage price increase does the Ministry consider acceptable for consumers to bear as a result of this scheme?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have indeed engaged with the producers, retailers and a variety of representatives representing all stakeholders, to understand what the dynamics are and what the concerns are.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The industry players, of course, are also concerned that they remain competitive within this industry.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will be monitoring the transition and how this process plays out.
